content.value_statement: Attendance data is hard to inspect when teams use Lark APIs directly. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through readonly attendance queries.
actual_capabilities: Guides lark-cli queries for personal attendance task records.
Requires schema lookup before native attendance API calls.
Applies employee_no as the fixed employee_type value.
Keeps user_ids empty when building attendance query data.
Identifies the readonly attendance scope for user_tasks.query.
limitations: Requires lark-cli to be installed and authenticated.
Does not modify attendance, approvals, shifts, or corrections.
Access depends on Lark tenant permissions and readonly scope grants.

use_cases.title: Check Personal Attendance
use_cases.description: Review recent clock records without browsing the Lark admin interface.

use_cases.title: Prepare Attendance Summaries
use_cases.description: Collect readonly attendance records before a weekly or monthly review.

use_cases.title: Validate API Usage
use_cases.description: Confirm required parameters and scopes before building an attendance workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Check This Week
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a short personal lookup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Lark attendance skill to check my attendance records for this week. Follow the schema before calling the API.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Date Range
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with a defined reporting period.
prompt_templates.prompt: Query my Lark attendance records for the selected date range. Summarize missing punches, late arrivals, and normal days.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Required Access
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup check before using the skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what Lark permission scope is required for attendance lookup and confirm whether the current access is readonly.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Monthly Summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a structured attendance review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Query my attendance records for the month and prepare a concise summary grouped by normal days, exceptions, and unresolved items.

output_examples.input: Check my attendance for this week.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes each workday, clock-in status, clock-out status, and any visible attendance exceptions.
The response lists dates with missing punches, late arrivals, or early departures, followed by a short review summary.

output_examples.input: What scope do I need for this lookup?
output_examples.output: The response explains that user_tasks.query requires the attendance task readonly scope in the Lark tenant.

best_practices: Run the schema lookup before every native attendance API call.
Use readonly access and request only the required date range.
Verify tenant permissions before interpreting missing or partial results.
anti_patterns: Do not guess attendance request fields without checking the schema.
Do not ask users for fixed employee_type or user_ids values.
Do not use this skill for attendance edits or approval actions.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps query personal Lark or Feishu attendance clock records through lark-cli.

faq.question: Does it change attendance records?
faq.answer: No. The documented method uses readonly attendance access.

faq.question: What tool must be installed?
faq.answer: The environment must provide lark-cli with valid Lark authentication.

faq.question: Which attendance API method is covered?
faq.answer: The skill documents user_tasks.query for attendance task lookup.

faq.question: Can it query another employee?
faq.answer: The skill describes personal attendance lookup. Access to other users depends on tenant permissions and policy.

faq.question: Why does it check the schema first?
faq.answer: Schema lookup reduces field mistakes and helps keep requests aligned with the current lark-cli interface.
